category.name: Loud Type Dept
category.description: Typography-first pages where giant, stretched or outlined letters carry the layout: brutalist grids, Klein-blue posters, variable-width stacks and Swiss grids. Little imagery, strong colour fields, and a clear grid or deliberate rawness. Best for festivals, foundries, archives, agencies and cultural venues that want to be read from across the room.

designs.name: Fileroom Brutalist Mono
designs.summary: Raw boxed layout with 4px black borders, giant Archivo Black headline, a safety-orange block, default blue links and hard-shadow stickers.

references.title: Brutalist website design guide with examples (Webflow)
Brutalist fonts in brutalist designs (Pangram Pangram)

designs.how_to_build: Wrap the page in a CSS grid with a 4px black border and give every cell a border instead of using gaps or shadows. Set the headline in Archivo Black at 170px or more with line-height .82 and tight negative tracking, and highlight one word with an inline-block coloured slab. Keep links as default blue underline and body text in a mono font, and add a single rotated sticker with a hard offset shadow.

designs.name: Full Volume Klein
designs.summary: A Klein-blue festival poster where three lines of Anton, solid then outlined, are scaled by script to fill the page edge to edge, with an orange marquee and ticket strip.

references.title: Brutalist typography posters gallery (Graphic Design Junction)

designs.how_to_build: Set each poster line in a condensed face, measure its natural width with getBoundingClientRect after fonts load, and scale font-size so every line spans the column exactly. Make the middle line transparent with -webkit-text-stroke in the paper colour. Keep colour to three flat values (blue, paper, orange) and anchor the bottom with a fixed-height info strip and a marquee band.

designs.name: Elastic Axis Stretch
designs.summary: A type foundry page where one word is stacked at four widths and weights along the variable font axes, each line fitted to the same column on a lilac ground.
keywords: width axis from condensed to extended

references.title: Brutalist fonts and variable type in practice (Pangram Pangram)
Typography and big-type shots on Dribbble (humanjpg)

designs.how_to_build: Load a variable font with both wdth and wght axes from Google Fonts. Render the same word several times, setting font-variation-settings per line, then measure each line as inline-block and scale its font-size to fill the column so narrower settings become taller. Label each line with its axis values in mono. Keep the palette to a single tint, black and one acid accent.

designs.name: Haus Nord Swiss Grid
designs.summary: A visible 12-column grid with a bleeding giant numeral, a concentric-arc motif in red and black, and tight Hanken Grotesk headlines for a concert series.

references.title: Mario Grgic Swiss-style web layouts on Dribbble
Readymag Almanac: grids in web design

designs.how_to_build: Define a 12-column CSS grid with 20px gaps and use subgrid so header and hero align to the same tracks. Draw the column hairlines as a decorative overlay. Set headlines at 118px and a bleeding 380px numeral with weight 900 and tracking of about -0.05em, and build the arc motif as inline SVG concentric circles with two filled sectors. Limit colour to red, black and off-white.
